newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - June 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - June 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Fears that Australia is headed for another drought were heightened yesterday when the National Climate Centre announced the El Nino weather pattern, associated with poor rainfall, is becoming entrenched. It is expected another drought would wipe A$500 million from Australia's rural export earnings. Page 3.

In response to an Australian Taxation Office report, which will result in the appointment of 900 field officers to watch businesses with a high incidence of cash transactions, Treasurer Peter Costello has endorsed a broad-based consumption tax to cut down on tax cheats. Costello said a GST would make it harder to avoid tax. Page 3.

Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston has said there will be a crack-down on pay TV and free-to-air broadcasters' sporting telecasts. It is believed hoarding is occurring, following the Nine Network's decision not to broadcast the first session o the first Ashes Test between Australia and England on free-to-air. Page 5.

The ALP is today expected to tell Prime Minister John Howard the Wik plan is 'unworkable', since they believe it will drive native title claimants back to the High Court for another challenge. This has raised the question of a double-dissolution election, with the ALP not revealing what parts of the legislation it would like to amend in the Senate. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Opposition Leader Kim Beazley has threatened his frontbench colleagues with the sack if they are found responsible for any "treachery" which could undermine Labor's ability to effectively combat the Howard Government. Beazley's comments are a response to recent concerns that Labor's ability to exploit the Government's recent difficulties is being compromised by internal bickering. Page 1.

National Australia Bank has been testing a new technology which allows customers to do their business through video contact with centralised bank staff. The innovative customer service system has been touted as a possible replacement for the now familiar automatic teller machines. Page 1.

Commonwealth Grants Commission Secretary Bob Searle has called for a review of the A$33 billion States grants system to be added to the Constitutional Convention Agenda. He claims such a move would establish better accountability for the delivery of Government services. Page 1.

An important visual arts event, the Sydney Biennial, went into voluntary administration last Friday following pressure from funding bodies for a board overhaul. The event's main sponsors - the New South Wales Government and Transfield Holdings - said they would withhold funding for 1998 until reforms have been implemented. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Speaking in response to a report by the Australian Tax Office on the "cash economy", Federal Treasurer Peter Costello claimed a goods and services tax was the most effective way to combat increasing tax avoidance and evasion. He told the Federal Opposition to 'stay tuned' for further Government moves on this issue. Page 1.

A study by Californian psychologist Judith Wallerstein has found that children continue to suffer emotional repercussions for at least 25 years after their parents divorce. Australian researcher Rosemary Dunlop however, says that the children of divorce are not identical and Americans should look at why some children cope and others do not. Page 1.

Chief Justice of the Family Court Alastair Nicholson, speaking at the Second World Congress on Family Law and the Rights of Children, yesterday condemned the Howard Government for failing to make a national apology over the 'stolen' Aboriginal children. Page 1.

The Bell's restaurant chain has closed, costing approximately 2,700 jobs country-wide. Bell's bought out 36 of Jardine Pacific's Sizzler restaurants for A$60 million in April, and renamed them. The closure, however, does not affect the 36 restaurants still trading under the Sizzler name as they are owned by a different company, Collins Food International. The company was negotiating to sell its interests to an American company within the next two weeks, and believes the old staff will be employed by that company. Page 1.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday initiated a new attack on violent crime announcing in Parliament that the Federal Government would commit A$13 million over three years to combat the problem. Emphasis will be given to research on the causes of crime and the ways they can be prevented. Page 1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett has awarded Adelaide artist Fiona Hall the inaugural State Contemporary visual art prize, worth A$100,000. However, Kennett liked another entry by Nigel Helyer, and has asked the director of the National Gallery of Victoria to purchase the piece. Page 1.

An investigation by the Age has revealed Victorian families now comprise one third of people looking for emergency accommodation. The State's families are also becoming homeless at a faster rate than any other Victorian group, with some welfare agencies reporting the number of families seeking shelter has risen six-fold in the past three years. Page 1.

The Victorian Opposition has labelled a proposal by the Government to allow schools more financial autonomy, including allowing them to borrow money, as 'postcode education'. Education unions and the Opposition believe it would widen the gap between rich and poor schools, with quality of education depending on the wealth of the school's community and suburb. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
